summary_html: Federal **Child and Family Services Reviews (CFSR)** monitor state performance on safety, permanency, and well-being. Project Milk Carton flags states that repeatedly fail or never publish CFSR improvement plans.

key_cases.holding: Except for narrowly defined statutory exceptions the state must have made reasonable efforts to reunify the family before parental rights are terminated, but the specific R.C. 2151.419(A)(1) reasonable-efforts determination applies only at the enumerated removal and disposition hearings and not at a hearing on an R.C. 2151.413 permanent-custody motion, where the agency must prove reasonable efforts only if it has not already done so.
key_cases.relevance: Reasonable-efforts findings are a CFSR measurement point, and this case defines when Ohio courts must make them.
key_cases.quote: we hold that, except for a few narrowly defined exceptions, the state must have made reasonable efforts to reunify the family prior to the termination of parental rights

key_cases.holding: An order that denies the agency's motion for permanent custody, terminates the agency's temporary custody and awards legal custody to a parent is a final, appealable order under R.C. 2505.02 because it affects the substantial rights of the parties and ends the proceeding.
key_cases.relevance: The 12-of-22 permanency clock discussed here is a core CFSR permanency measure.
key_cases.quote: In contrast, a parent does have a substantial right in the custody of his or her child.

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Cincinnati Enquirer v. Jones-Kelley
key_cases.holding: The Court granted mandamus compelling the Department of Job and Family Services to release a requested database, holding the custodian failed to carry its burden of showing the records fell squarely within a statutory exception and that a later amendment excluding foster-caregiver information did not apply retroactively.
key_cases.relevance: Performance monitoring depends on the state-level data this case made accessible.
key_cases.quote: A custodian does not meet this burden if it has not proven that the requested records fall squarely within the exception.
